terms.p: A cost that is occasionally large but averages out small across a run of operations, which is why growing a Vec one push at a time is still linear overall.
Asking the allocator for a larger block, copying every element into it and freeing the old one, which is what a Vec does when it runs out of capacity.
The hash function a Rust HashMap uses by default, seeded randomly at startup so that an attacker cannot craft keys that all collide.
HashMap::entry, which hands you the slot for a key whether or not anything is in it, so look-up-then-insert-then-update costs a single hash.
One fixed allocation with a head and a tail index that wrap around to the start, giving constant-time insertion and removal at both ends without shifting anything.
